claim: For Godot art-import validation, raw PNG presence is not enough; the package must include Godot import metadata and a clean runtime load check.
context: During Phase 3F, Implementation copied prepared transparent PNGs into the Godot project and referenced them from main.tscn. The first smoke command exited 0 but printed loader errors because the PNGs had not been imported by Godot. Running godot --headless --path game --import generated .png.import metadata, after which clean smoke output and headless scene execution passed.

evidence.summary: The implementation Run records the initial No loader found errors, the godot --import recovery, generated .png.import files, and final clean smoke/headless runtime success.
QA independently confirmed source PNGs, .png.import metadata, Texture2D/Sprite2D scene wiring, clean smoke output, and headless scene execution.
The implementation Work Package required imported asset files, scene references, clean smoke output, and headless main scene execution without gameplay changes.
The QA Run repeated clean smoke and headless scene checks after artifact creation and found no runtime resource-load errors.

applies_when: Prototype or production art assets are copied into a Godot project.
A scene references imported textures through res:// asset paths.
The phase gate depends on proving that generated or prepared art can load in the engine.
does_not_apply_when: The asset is not intended to be loaded by Godot.
The task is only visual review outside the engine.
The project uses a different engine or a custom import pipeline with different metadata rules.

reuse_rule: When validating Godot asset import, check for source files, tracked .import metadata, clean smoke output with no engine error lines, and a headless scene run before claiming the art package is engine-loadable.
promotion_note: Candidate only. Promotion should wait until another Godot asset-import workflow repeats the same metadata/runtime requirement or Phase 4 adopts it as a standard gate.
